source_document.body:
Niron Magnetics will build a $1.8 billion manufacturing campus in Dothan, Alabama, to make rare-earth-free permanent magnets at high volume. Gov. Kay Ivey announced the project on Nov. 20.
What’s Related
The 1.6-million-square-foot campus will go on the Westgate Super Site, a 446-acre industrial park in Houston County. The plant is designed to make 10,000 tons of magnets a year and is expected to create about 700 high-wage jobs within five years. Construction is set to start in 2028, and production should begin in 2029.
Niron is a Minneapolis company founded in 2013. It makes Iron Nitride magnets from abundant domestic materials and pitches them as a lower-cost alternative to neodymium magnets, which rely on rare earths. Its magnets go into AI infrastructure , cars, industrial equipment, and consumer electronics .
“Alabama has demonstrated time and time again that when it comes to competing for the world's most transformative industries, we are second to none,” Ivey said.
Why Dothan won out
Niron looked at a lot of options before it landed in the Wiregrass.
“Every step of the way, Alabama treated our success as its own,” said Niron CEO Jonathan Rowntree. “We considered sites in 22 states, and Alabama stood out from the very first conversation.”
The site was ready for a project like this. The City of Dothan, Houston County, the city's Industrial Development Board, and the Dothan Area Chamber of Commerce spent several years developing it. It got funding from the state's SEEDS site program in 2024 and later from the Growing Alabama Tax Credit program. The park also has a CSX rail line and earned CSX Select Site Platinum status in late 2025. Real estate firm Savills advised Niron on the search.
A much bigger second plant
Dothan will be home to Niron's second high-volume plant. The first one, in Sartell, Minnesota, opens in 2027 and can make up to 1,500 tons of magnets a year. The Alabama plant is designed to make more than six times that amount.
According to the state, about 90% of global rare-earth magnet production happens overseas. Officials say the Dothan plant will help build up U.S. supply chains for automotive , advanced technology , and defense.
Dothan Mayor Mark Saliba said the payoff for local families is the big story.
“This project means opportunity,” Saliba said. “It means families can build their futures here with state-of-the-art technology that will strengthen America's supply chain and our national security , which our country depends on.”
